tasks.short: Develop and deliver training on pay, benefits and job evaluation.

steps.what: Gather approved policies, recurring questions and previous training feedback.
Agree learning objectives, audience needs and examples with the training specialist.
Write lesson plans, presentation materials, exercises and knowledge checks.

loop.input: Training brief and versioned, approved training source pack.
loop.output: Training draft with source references for policy claims.
loop.check: Check source versions, required sections and references; specialist checks meaning and exercises.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision attempts per module; unresolved claims return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but adapting explanations and exercises requires language generation.

steps.what: Review policy accuracy and approve the training materials.
Publish the course, enrol participants and schedule live sessions.
Teach the session, discuss examples and answer sensitive pay or benefits questions.
Record attendance and knowledge checks, then collect participant feedback.

tasks.design: A source-pack builder reads approved versions from the {DOCS}; a bounded drafting loop fills reusable lesson templates. The compensation specialist approves materials before configured flows in the {LMS} and {CALENDAR} publish and schedule them. Live teaching remains human, supported by prepared examples and automatically collected completion records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source gathering and course formatting took time, while generic templates rarely matched the audience or policy wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing course workflows handle administration. AI-assisted coding makes source collection and template assembly cheaper; bounded drafting adapts approved explanations.
tasks.still_hard: Good examples, sensitive questions and checking policy meaning still need expertise. GDPR applies to learner records; national rules may affect mandatory training and consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise confusion, explain trade-offs and make employees comfortable asking questions about pay.

ambition.what: A short benefits induction for shift workers who miss office-hour sessions.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less course assembly and scheduling, with more time for teaching and checking understanding. The specialist gains discretion over lesson formats within approved policy; policy decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Design practical exercises and assess learning.
reach.learn: Adult learning, accessible materials and knowledge checks that reveal misunderstandings.

evidence.claim: Course enrolment, completion tracking and template assembly are established software capabilities.
Drafting from approved sources can reduce preparation, but instructional quality still needs specialist review.
The digest documents fabricated citations in a generated report, supporting explicit source checks for policy materials.

assumptions: The pilot covers one training programme and one language.
Approved policy versions and reusable course templates are available.
The time split retains substantial creative and teaching work, consistent with the supplied priors.
Build ranges are estimates, include applicable consultation work, and exclude unpredictable external waiting.
unknowns: Which enrolment, attendance and feedback features the current {LMS} supports.
Whether policy documents have reliable approval and version metadata.
Whether shift workers can access learning during paid working time.
research_questions: Which exercises improve understanding of benefits choices without collecting sensitive personal examples?
Which national rules apply to mandatory training records and employee consultation?
new_work: Review generated lessons and verify policy references.
Resolve unanswered questions from live sessions.
Refresh source mappings and exercises when policy changes.
Check that automatic completion records reflect actual participation.

tasks.short: Maintain personnel records and keep employee handbooks current.

steps.what: Receive approved personnel changes and policy revisions through forms and the shared mailbox.
Check employee identity, effective dates, approvals and required fields against existing records.
Update personnel fields and file approved supporting documents.
Identify handbook sections affected by the approved policy revision.

loop.input: Approved policy revision and current employee handbook.
loop.output: Affected sections with quoted source passages and proposed change scope.
loop.check: Verify section identifiers and quotations; specialist checks omitted cross-references.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction attempt per revision; uncertain scope returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search misses paraphrases and policy dependencies across free-text sections.

steps.what: Draft handbook amendments and assemble the revised version.

loop.input: Reviewed handbook change map, approved policy and handbook template.
loop.output: Handbook draft with tracked amendments and source references.
loop.check: Check unchanged sections, dates and references; specialist reviews obligations and wording.
loop.stop: One draft and two revision attempts; unresolved contradictions remain flagged for human editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Document assembly is deterministic, but coherent amendments require reading and rewriting policy prose.

steps.what: Approve the handbook revision after required legal review and employee consultation.
Publish the approved handbook, archive the superseded version and request acknowledgements where needed.
Compare record changes and handbook acknowledgements with outstanding requests.

tasks.design: Configure structured change requests and validation in the {WORKFLOW} and {HCM}, with approved documents retained in the {DOCS}. A bounded reading and drafting loop prepares handbook amendments for an HR manager's approval; configured publication then distributes that approved version. A reconciliation job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feeds outstanding changes and acknowledgements to the {BI}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes arrived in inconsistent messages, approval evidence was scattered, and handbook cross-references required manual reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record workflows can enforce required fields and approval references. Small integrations and bounded document loops are cheaper to build and maintain with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting effective dates, retention rules and policy changes remain difficult. GDPR and national consultation rules apply; handbook acknowledgement does not establish consent to contractual changes.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently clerical update changes an employee's rights or needs explanation.

ambition.what: A dated policy-change summary showing employees which handbook sections changed.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying records and formatting documents to resolving exceptions and explaining policy changes. The specialist can manage the approved revision schedule; authority to change employment terms remains with the authorised decision makers.

reach.task: Manage effective-dated records and document retention.
reach.learn: Record provenance, access permissions and correction procedures.

reach.task: Prepare consultation material for handbook changes.
reach.learn: Which changes require consultation and what evidence must be retained.

evidence.claim: Structured record updates, version control and exception reconciliation are established deterministic capabilities.
Bounded drafting can prepare handbook amendments; it does not establish their legal validity.
In the Netherlands, some HR data and monitoring arrangements require works council consent; other countries need a national assessment.

assumptions: Personnel changes already carry the required substantive approval before record entry.
Routine updates use structured forms; ambiguous mailbox requests become exceptions.
The pilot covers one handbook and a limited set of personnel fields.
Build ranges include access and applicable consultation work; formal consultation may take longer.
The transformation-heavy prior fits records, while handbook approval remains substantive human work.
unknowns: Which fields have effective dates, audit trails and configurable validation in the {HCM}.
Whether personnel records and handbook documents share stable identifiers.
Which national consultation arrangements and retention schedules apply.
How many incoming changes lack valid approval evidence.
research_questions: Which handbook changes alter contractual obligations under the relevant national rules?
How should access and retention differ between personnel documents and published handbook versions?
new_work: Resolve rejected changes and conflicting effective dates.
Review handbook change maps and draft amendments.
Maintain field validation, access permissions and retention rules.
Investigate reconciliation failures and publication errors.

tasks.short: Design merit and incentive programmes, coordinate awards and prepare approved payroll changes.

steps.what: Export workforce, current pay, performance and budget data for the compensation cycle.
Reconcile employee identifiers, eligibility dates, currencies and pay components.
Model merit matrices, incentive formulas, budget costs and distribution effects.
Develop the programme proposal and discuss incentives, affordability and fairness with decision makers.
Approve programme rules and budget after required consultation.
Propose individual awards and justify departures from the approved guidelines.
Review award exceptions, budget totals and unexplained differences between comparable employee groups.
Approve final awards and documented exceptions within delegated authority.
Prepare approved award changes for payroll and check the import result.
Prepare award letters and distribute them through approved employee communication channels.

tasks.design: A governed job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles inputs from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL}, {TALENT} and {ERP}, then calculates programme scenarios for the {BI}. Configure proposal forms and separate programme and award approvals in the {HCM} and {WORKFLOW}. Only approved awards enter the {PAYROLL} change batch and populate fixed letters in the {DOCS}; payroll release retains its existing approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cross-system identifiers, changing pay components and local programme rules made integrations expensive. Choosing incentives and approving awards also requires accountable judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building connectors, calculation tests and reconciliation views. Established compensation forms and approval workflows can handle the cycle without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable comparators, incentive side effects and contested awards remain difficult. GDPR, equal-pay obligations and national employment and consultation rules constrain data use and changes.
tasks.human_edge: Anticipate how incentives change behaviour and defend fair, affordable choices to employees and managers.

ambition.what: A quarterly incentive-design review using actual costs and payout distributions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reconciliation and workbook repair to scenario discussions and exception resolution. With delegated authority, the specialist can convene quarterly design reviews and recommend adjustments; final budget and award authority stays with designated approvers.

reach.task: Evaluate incentive design against business objectives.
reach.learn: Behavioural effects, affordability and how to present competing programme options.

reach.task: Validate compensation changes before a pay run.
reach.learn: Effective dates, pay-component mappings and import reconciliation.

evidence.claim: Eligibility calculations, merit matrices, budget checks and approved-letter generation can use deterministic rules.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment where individual pay decisions would be solely automated and significantly affect employees.
An AI system evaluating workers or affecting employment terms may fall within the AI Act's employment category; intended use needs assessment.

assumptions: The pilot covers one compensation cycle, currency and approved rule set.
Human managers supply performance judgements; the proposed solution does not generate worker scores.
Programme rules specify rounding, eligibility, effective dates and exception authority.
The creative and decision-heavy prior remains relevant despite substantial deterministic administration.
Build ranges include access and applicable consultation work; external approval timelines may exceed them.
unknowns: Whether the {HCM} includes configurable compensation planning and approval features.
Which pay components and identifiers agree across the {HCM} and {PAYROLL}.
Who has delegated authority for programme rules, budgets and individual exceptions.
Which employee comparison data can lawfully be used for distribution checks.
research_questions: Which incentive formulas create unintended behaviour under realistic operating scenarios?
Which national consultation and equal-pay requirements apply to programme changes?
Which validation controls detect incorrect effective dates and duplicate payroll changes?
new_work: Maintain eligibility rules and pay-component mappings.
Review reconciliation failures and unusual payout distributions.
Test rule changes against historical and boundary cases.
Check approval evidence and payroll import results.
Monitor actual incentive costs and behavioural effects.

tasks.short: Evaluate jobs, assign grades and recommend salary and applicable working-time coverage.

steps.what: Receive the job evaluation request and gather the current role description and organisation context.
Interview the line manager and job holder to establish actual duties and responsibilities.
Organise evidence by evaluation factor and identify missing or contradictory information.

loop.input: Job description, interview notes and approved evaluation-factor definitions.
loop.output: Evidence table containing source passages, factor labels and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Verify quotations and source locations; specialist checks placement and completeness. No inferred duties or scores.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt per job; unresolved gaps return for human clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant duties appear in varied prose and interview notes, so fixed field mappings are insufficient.

steps.what: Determine collective-agreement and working-time coverage under the applicable national rules.
Rate evaluation factors and compare the job with established benchmark roles.
Challenge the evaluation and approve the grade and coverage assessment.
Recommend a salary range or salary using approved bands and relevant market comparisons.
Approve the salary recommendation or refer an exception to the authorised decision maker.
Record approved classification and salary decisions, then notify the requesting manager.

tasks.design: Configure job intake and decision records in the {WORKFLOW} and {HCM}, with evidence retained in the {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop organises source passages for specialist evaluation; deterministic calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} produce salary-band comparisons in the {BI}. Separate classification and salary approvals unlock record updates and notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: Role descriptions used inconsistent language, evidence was dispersed, and factor ratings depended on tacit calibration between evaluators.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can organise prose without deciding the grade. AI-assisted coding makes evidence tables, comparison calculations and approval links cheaper to implement.
tasks.still_hard: Actual duties may differ from written descriptions, and contested grading requires careful calibration. There is no universal European exempt/non-exempt split: coverage follows national rules and collective agreements. GDPR applies, and AI used to evaluate workers or affect employment terms needs an AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish the value of a job from the influence of its holder or manager, and explain a defensible comparison.

ambition.what: An early job-design consultation for managers before a new role is approved.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence sorting and record entry, with more time for interviews, calibration and job-design advice. The specialist can offer earlier classification advice; binding grade and salary decisions retain their explicit approval routes.

reach.task: Review whether job evaluation factors disadvantage comparable groups.
reach.learn: Gender-neutral factor definitions, comparator selection and bias in job descriptions.

reach.task: Design roles and reporting structures before recruitment.
reach.learn: Organisation design, responsibility boundaries and how role changes affect grading.

evidence.claim: Evidence extraction, factor-score arithmetic and salary-band comparisons can be separated from human classification decisions.
Job or worker evaluation that affects employment terms needs assessment against the AI Act employment category.
GDPR Article 22 is relevant if classification or salary decisions become solely automated with significant effects.
The digest identifies gender-neutral job evaluation as a pay-transparency requirement; national implementation needs checking.

assumptions: An approved job evaluation framework and benchmark roles already exist.
The pilot covers one national jurisdiction and job family.
Market pay data is licensed for the proposed use.
The loop extracts evidence only; it does not rate workers or assign grades.
The judgement-heavy prior is retained; gains chiefly come from preparation, comparisons and recording.
Build ranges include applicable consultation and access work; external waiting may extend rollout.
unknowns: Which evaluation framework, collective agreements and national rules apply.
How consistently evaluators currently rate the same job evidence.
Whether benchmark jobs and salary bands are current and approved.
Which classification and salary decisions require additional approval or an appeal route.
research_questions: Can evaluators reproduce factor ratings when given the same evidence table?
Which national provisions determine working-time and collective-agreement coverage?
Does the intended extraction-only use fall within the relevant AI Act category?
new_work: Check extracted evidence and resolve missing duties.
Maintain benchmark roles and salary-band data.
Calibrate evaluators and review contested classifications.
Monitor whether evidence extraction systematically omits particular kinds of work.
Maintain decision records and handle appeals.

role.altitude: The role spends less time assembling documents, moving records and repairing calculations, and more time explaining pay choices, testing programme design and calibrating jobs. Additional decision rights require explicit delegation; the technology mainly improves the evidence and timing of recommendations.
reach: Training and development specialists: practical learning design and accessible benefits education.
Payroll and timekeeping clerks: effective-dated changes and payroll reconciliation.
Labor relations specialists: consultation preparation and collective-agreement interpretation.
Equal opportunity representatives: fair comparators and gender-neutral job evaluation.
Human resources managers: early role design and organisation planning.
skills_to_grow: Translate approved policy into testable calculation and validation rules.
Trace data and documents to their approved source versions.
Design compensation scenarios and explain incentive trade-offs.
Calibrate job evaluation and distinguish jobs from individual performance.
Review bounded model outputs for omissions and unsupported claims.
Understand GDPR, relevant AI Act uses and applicable national employment rules.
role.ambitious_version: Provide an early reward-and-job-design advisory service: managers receive defensible role comparisons, affordable incentive scenarios and clear employee explanations before decisions are committed.

job.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
